panels.title: Why quick war failed
ascii_lines: MARNE, SEPT 1914 -> German advance halted
DEFENSIVE FIREPOWER -> movement cannot exploit success
TRENCHES -> western front hardens
RESULT -> strategy shifts from manoeuvre to endurance
MUST REMEMBER: Mobilisation and stalemate in 1914, total-war economies, multiple European and
imperial fronts, US entry and Russian exit in 1917, and the November 1918 armistice must
remain chronologically distinct.

imperial fronts, US entry and Russian exit in 1917, and the November 1918 armistice must
remain chronologically distinct.
source_references: Marne and the failure of quick victory

panels.title: Attrition battlefield
ascii_lines: VERDUN 1916 -> prolonged exhaustion
SOMME 1916 -> huge cost and limited ground
DEFENCE -> machine-guns and artillery dominate
STRATEGIC TEST -> manpower, industry and morale

panels.title: Sea-war mechanism
ascii_lines: BRITISH FLEET -> blockade Central Powers
JUTLAND -> no decisive tactical resolution
GERMAN U-BOATS -> unrestricted campaign
CONVOYS -> shipping losses reduced; British control survives
source_references: The submarine gamble and American entry

panels.title: 1917 strategic exchange
ascii_lines: RUSSIA -> revolution and exit reduce Germany's eastern burden
USA -> entry adds finance, food, shipping, morale and troops
GERMAN GAMBLE -> submarine warfare helps trigger US entry
NET EFFECT -> American resources offset Russian withdrawal
source_references: The submarine gamble and American entry

panels.title: How the Central Powers lost
ascii_lines: TWO FRONTS -> Germany's structural burden
BLOCKADE -> supplies and civilian endurance weaken
1918 OFFENSIVE -> Ludendorff fails
ALLIES COLLAPSE -> Bulgaria, Habsburg and Ottoman systems fall
source_references: Ludendorff fails and Allied unity improves

panels.title: Total-war society
ascii_lines: STATE -> controls industry, transport and food
WOMEN -> enter expanded wartime production roles
CIVILIANS -> blockade and propaganda make home front strategic
EMPIRE -> colonial manpower and territory globalise the war

panels.title: Political earthquake
ascii_lines: RUSSIA -> Bolshevik rule
GERMANY -> revolution and Weimar Republic
HABSBURG/OTTOMAN -> empires collapse into new arrangements
GLOBAL POWER -> USA and Japan gain as Europe weakens

panels.title: Five-treaty matching
ascii_lines: VERSAILLES -> Germany; ST GERMAIN -> Austria
TRIANON -> Hungary; NEUILLY -> Bulgaria
SEVRES -> Ottoman Turkey, rejected
LAUSANNE 1923 -> revised Turkish settlement
source_references: The settlement as five treaty routes

panels.title: Versailles containment
ascii_lines: TERRITORY -> Alsace-Lorraine, Poland, Danzig, Saar
MILITARY -> 100,000 army; no conscription or key weapons
RHINELAND -> demilitarised
AUSTRIA -> union with Germany forbidden

panels.title: Article 231 and reparations
ascii_lines: ARTICLE 231 -> legal liability for Allied loss and damage
POLITICS -> read in Germany as war-guilt clause
1921 -> reparations fixed at £6600 million
EFFECT -> revisionist grievance plus enforcement problem
CLOSE DISTINCTION: Military victory, armistice, Paris peace treaties, Versailles provisions
and the League settlement were separate stages; treaty grievance neither explains the whole
war nor makes a second war automatic.
CLOSE DISTINCTION: Military victory, armistice, Paris peace treaties, Versailles provisions
and the League settlement were separate stages; treaty grievance neither explains the whole
war nor makes a second war automatic.

panels.title: Mandates: change and continuity
ascii_lines: OLD LANGUAGE -> conquest and annexation
NEW LANGUAGE -> League trusteeship and preparation for independence
PRACTICE -> Britain and France retain imperial control
VERDICT -> empire survives under conditional justification
EVIDENCE LIMIT: Mass death, revolution, empire collapse, mandates, minority problems and
colonial mobilisation remade the world beyond Europe, so aftermath cannot be reduced to
German punishment alone.

panels.title: War-and-peace answer spine
ascii_lines: COURSE -> failed quick war, attrition, blockade and coalition collapse
TOTAL WAR -> state, society, women, civilians and empire
SETTLEMENT -> treaty cluster, League, mandates and minorities
VERDICT -> political earthquake followed by unstable peace
